severity_levels.blocking: A violation should stop generation, validation, approval, or publish for the mapped stage.
severity_levels.must: A required rule that should be enforced whenever that rule set is loaded.
severity_levels.should: A strong default that may be overridden by explicit client, account, style-pack, or user direction if still safe.
severity_levels.preference: A default taste or quality preference that should not block generation by itself.

rule_sets.title: Brand Safety Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage creates story facts, captions, visual plans, or publish-facing copy.

rules.text: Do not invent facts, quotes, names, locations, dates, motives, outcomes, product claims, metrics, endorsements, or source URLs not supported by the input payload.
For harm, abuse, violence, coercion, victim testimony, or similar sensitive topics, keep wording and imagery trauma-informed, non-graphic, non-sexualized, and non-sensational.
Keep current pipeline outputs in English unless a later architecture change explicitly adds multilingual support.
Avoid spammy, deceptive, guaranteed-result, clickbait, or false-scarcity language.
Prefer concise, credible, mobile-native language unless a style pack or client profile intentionally chooses a different safe voice.

rule_sets.title: Visual Consistency Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage plans scene visuals, image/video prompts, cover prompts, or render-facing metadata.

rules.text: Generated visuals must not request visible text, typography, subtitles, captions, labels, logos, UI, watermarks, signage, documents, newspapers, placards, speech bubbles, or other readable text elements.

Scene 1 must use face-image/title-card metadata only: `is_face_image=true`, `asset_type=image`, `face_image_title` of 2-5 words, duration 4 seconds or less; the generated image prompt itself remains text-free.
Scenes after scene 1 must not carry a face-image title and should normally use video assets unless a specific safe exception is supplied.
Every visual prompt must identify a concrete focal subject, action or situation, setting, and story-specific evidence tied to the matching narration beat.
Preserve the selected visual style contract across scenes unless safety or factual boundaries require a change.
Prefer documentary-realistic, mobile-readable compositions unless the selected style pack calls for a different safe visual treatment.

rule_sets.title: Voice Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage writes narration, dialogue lines, TTS instructions, or voice performance metadata.

rules.text: `dialogue_lines` must match or cleanly slice from the spoken `narration_text` for the same scene, without missing or reordered narration beats.
Preserve a clean human-readable narration script; provider-specific emotion syntax belongs in delivery metadata where possible.
Each scene should carry narration-aligned delivery or TTS instructions that describe emotion, pacing, and energy without changing the facts.
Keep narration breathable for a spoken Reel: vary sentence length and avoid long run-on passages.
Prefer grounded human delivery over announcer-style narration unless the selected style pack intentionally calls for a more performed voice.

rule_sets.title: Music and SFX Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage creates music direction, SFX cues, render audio metadata, or music licensing decisions.

rules.text: Unknown or unclear music/SFX license status must block publish until resolved.
Default background music should be subtle, instrumental, and low enough to sit under narration; vocals require explicit creative direction and licensing confidence.
Scene music and SFX cues should match local emotional intensity without overpowering the spoken story.

rule_sets.title: Avatar Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage selects, describes, or routes an avatar, presenter, or likeness-based asset.

rules.text: Do not use a real person's likeness, voice, or implied endorsement without explicit consent metadata.
Synthetic avatar routes must remain transparent and must not pretend to be an unrecorded real-person message.
Prefer non-avatar visuals unless the task, client profile, or style pack clearly calls for an avatar route.

rule_sets.title: Editing Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage sets scene timing, pacing, transitions, subtitle metadata, or render seed data.

rules.text: Scene timings must be contiguous, start near 0 seconds, have positive durations, and end close to the target duration.
Subtitles are metadata only in the current pipeline; `render_manifest_seed_json.subtitles.enabled` must be false unless a later renderer contract changes this.
Do not add, remove, or reorder scenes when a prior scene guide or director contract already defines scene count and numbering.
Transitions should support pacing and comprehension; avoid decorative transition choices that distract from narration.
Prefer simple cuts, match cuts, or soft cuts unless a style pack calls for more expressive editing.

rule_sets.title: Provider Routing Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage chooses models, providers, adapters, host providers, or render providers.

rules.text: If a selected provider is not implemented for a component, fail fast instead of silently falling back to a different provider.
Provider-specific responses must be normalized to the repo's stable asset, script, storyboard, render, or cost shape before downstream use.
Keep provider branching in helper scripts/adapters, not scattered through n8n workflow JSON.
Do not call paid external APIs for documentation, fixture, or contract-only sessions.

rule_sets.title: Platform Publishing Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage prepares captions, hashtags, publish rows, media URLs, or live publish actions.

rules.text: Live publish must not run unless the explicit publish enable flag and required Instagram credentials are present in runtime configuration.
Publishable media URLs must be public HTTPS URLs and must not point to local-only or private network hosts.
Do not publish if existing platform media IDs or published timestamps indicate the content was already published.
Keep caption copy and hashtags cleanly separated until final composition for the platform.

rule_sets.title: Approval Rules
rule_sets.read_when: Any stage validates final packages, marks approval status, selects final render output, or gates publish.

rules.text: Once selected-video approval is implemented, publish must require the approved selected render, not merely any successful render.
Reject or block packages with missing script, storyboard, visual assets, narration assets, render output, caption, or required license metadata.
Live publish paths should preserve an explicit review/approval step when a workflow is intended for public posting.
Approval or rejection should record a concise review note for auditability.
